About the Report 
NLC India Limited (NLCIL) is pleased to present its fourth Integrated Report, providing a comprehensive overview 
of	the	organisation’s	financial	and	non-financial	performance	for	FY	2024-25.	This	report	highlights	the	progress	made,	key	achievements,	and	initiatives	undertaken	by	NLCIL	throughout	the	year,	offering	stakeholders	valuable	insights	to	inform	their	decision-making	processes.	This	report	reflects	the	organisation’s	dedication	to	fostering	long-term	growth	and	promoting	responsible	business	practices	in	response	to	the	evolving	industry	dynamics.
Reporting Scope and Boundary 
Spanning	the	reporting	period	from	April	1,	2024	to	March	31,	2025,	this	report	offers	a	comprehensive	analysis	of	the	
NLCIL	Group,	encompassing	its	Subsidiaries,	Associates	and	Joint	Ventures.	For	the	current	fiscal	year,	the	Group	comprises	5	Subsidiaries,	2	Joint	Ventures	and	2	Step-down	subsidiary	Companies.

Data Management
At NLCIL, we follow a carefully structured and uniformly 
applied process across all our operational sites for the collection, measurement, calculation, and analysis of performance	metrics.	This	rigorous	methodology	ensures	the accuracy, reliability, and consistency of data, supporting effective	decision-making	and	strategic	initiatives.
Responsibility Statement
NLCIL is steadfast in its commitment to providing precise	and	comprehensive	information	on	its	financial,	Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG), and operational	performance	to	all	stakeholders.	The	creation	of this report stems from extensive consultations across all business units and departments within the organisation, enriched	with	critical	governance	insights.	The	Board	and Management jointly bear responsibility for ensuring the integrity, impartiality, transparency, and equitable presentation	of	the	information	within	this	report.
Assurance
This report delivers a thorough account of the Group’s operations,	integrating	both	financial	and	non-financial	data.	The	financial	details,	encompassing	both	consolidated	and standalone accounts, have undergone a meticulous audit by	M/s.	Sundaram	&	Srinivasan,	Chartered	Accountants	and	M/s.	Chaturvedi	&	Co	LLP,	Chartered	Accountants.	This	dual-audit	approach	has	been	adopted	to	affirm	the	credibility	and	accuracy	of	the	financial	information	shared.Forward-looking Statements 
Some portions of this report may feature forward-looking statements, recognisable by terms such as ‘may’, ‘expects’, ‘could’,	‘intends’,	‘aims’,	or	similar	expressions.	These	statements rely on assumptions and methodologies that entail a level of judgement and inherent uncertainties, beyond	our	control.	Therefore,	actual	results	may	differ,	and we cannot ensure the accuracy or realisation of these predictions	due	to	the	uncertainties	involved.	While	we	consider the assumptions underlying these statements to be sound, such assumptions may not hold, leading to alternative	outcomes.
Feedback
NLCIL remains dedicated to fostering open, transparent communication with its stakeholders across all touchpoints, ensuring	prompt	and	efficient	support	for	their	needs	and	concerns.	Shareholders	and	investors	are	encouraged	to	reach out to the Company Secretary at either the registered office	or	corporate	address.	For	immediate	issue	resolution,	investors may also contact Integrated Registry Management Services Private Limited, NLCIL’s trusted Registrar & Share	Transfer	Agent.

Message from the Chairman & Managing Director
FY 2024–25 was a landmark year for NLCIL, 
marked by record lignite and coal production, commissioning of Unit-I at Ghatampur Thermal Power Station, robust renewable energy progress, and highest-ever capex of	₹7,736	crore.	Revenue	grew	17.55%	to	₹15,283	crore,	with	record	PAT	of	₹2,714	crore.	Strategic expansions in mining, renewables, and critical minerals strengthened our future readiness.	Looking	ahead,	we	are	on	course	to	achieve	104.35	MTPA	mining	capacity,	over 10 GW each in thermal and renewable power by 2030, while advancing green hydrogen, battery storage, and sustainability initiatives—driving energy security and a cleaner,	inclusive	future	for	India.
Prasanna Kumar Motupalli

Message from the Chairman & Managing Director
We have demonstrated the capacity to overcome challenges 
and create value for stakeholders while positioning ourselves to capitalise on the immense opportunities that lie ahead in India’s	energy	sector.
India’s peak power demand touched record highs of 
over	250	GW	in	FY	2024-25,	reaffirming	the	critical	role	of NLCIL in ensuring energy security while supporting the nation’s renewable energy transition in line with COP	commitments.
Performance Highlights
Operational Performance
The performance of NLCIL during FY 2024-25 has been exemplary, registering robust growth across our core businesses.	Our	lignite	and	coal	production	grew	by	14% 	
over	the	previous	year.	This	was	led	by	focused	operational 	
improvements and a resolution of long-standing challenges, 
Dear Shareholders,
It is with great pride and 
optimism that I present to you the performance and progress of your Company for FY 2024-25, a year that marked a decisive phase in	our	journey	of	growth.	It has been a year of renewed momentum, resilience and strategic	readiness.especially	in	land	acquisition	at	Neyveli.	Notably,	the 	
Talabira	II	&	III	coal	mine	achieved	17.2	Million	Tonnes 	
Per	Annum	(MTPA)	production,	a	remarkable	36% 	
increase over last year, solidifying its role as a cornerstone 
of	our	fuel	security	strategy.
A	major	modification	has	been	carried	out	in	Thermal 	
Power Station II Expansion Fluidised Bed Heat 
Exchangers, to improve the power generation, and it	is	expected	to	significantly	improve	the	long-term 	
performance	and	reliability	of	the	plant.	Importantly, 	
most of our other generating units not only reached the targets	but	overshot	them.	A	milestone	achievement	this 	
year was the commissioning of Unit-I of Ghatampur Thermal Power Station (GTPS) in December 2024, which	has	already	contributed	around	1.2	BU	by	the	end 	
of	March	2025.	This	feat	has	enabled	your	Company	to 	
join	the	elite	club	of	supercritical	thermal	operations. 	
NLCIL	is	poised	to	set	new	benchmarks	in	efficient 	
and	sustainable	thermal	power	generation.
We also took decisive industry-backed business decisions 
to address long-standing challenges for the renewable energy	sector.	These	proactive	measures	have	improved 	
confidence	among	Solar	Developer	Operators	(SDOs) 	
and O&M contractors, setting the stage for accelerated capacity	addition	and	improved	operational	efficiency 	
in	the	years	ahead.
As a part of expanding RE and new business ventures, 
your Company has signed Joint Venture Agreements with State Government PSEs of Assam, Rajasthan and Maharashtra and in short span of time formed joint	ventures	viz.	‘NIRL	Assam	Renewables	Limited 	
(NARL)’, ‘NLC Rajasthan Power Limited (NRPL)’ &	‘NIRL	Rajasthan	Renewables	Limited	(NRRL)’.
These developments have laid a strong foundation 
for	realising	NLCIL’s	ambitious	Vision	2030	targets: 	
doubling thermal and mining capacities, and achieving a	multifold	increase	in	renewable	energy	capacity. 	
Specifically,	the	company	is	on	track	to	reach	10	GW	of 	
thermal	capacity,	10.1	GW	of	renewable	energy	capacity, 	
and	over	104.35	MTPA	in	mining	capacity	by	2030.
FY 2024-25 has, therefore, been a year of expansion and 
transformation.	We	have	laid	the	foundation	for	a	positive 	
and sustained upward trajectory in our production and performance	curve.	Looking	forward,	the	actions	initiated 	
this	year	will	yield	significant	results	on	the	long	run	and 	
we	are	confident	of	creating	new	records	in	lignite	and 	
coal mining, power generation and renewable energy integration	in	the	years	to	come.Financial Performance
The	year	under	review	witnessed	significant	progress	across our strategic priorities and operational excellence, translating	into	strong	financial	performance.	Revenue	from	operations	grew	by	17.55%	to	₹15,283	crore	in	FY	2024-25,	compared	to	₹13,001	crore	in	FY	2023-24.	We	reported	our	highest-ever	EBITDA	of	₹6,513	crore	(₹5,556	crore	in FY 2023-24) and delivered all time highest ever PAT of	₹2,714	crore,	up	from	₹1,868	crore	in	the	previous	year	and this has resulted in substantial increase of Earnings Per	Share.	Market	capitalisation	has	touched	its	all	time	high	of	more	than	₹43,000	crore.
Your Company has been granted Capital Gains Tax 
exemption under Section 47 (viiaf) of the Income Tax Act, 1961, in respect of the transfer of renewable energy assets	to	NIRL	by	the	Ministry	of	Finance.
Your Company has been granted approval to invest upto 
₹7,000	crore	in	various	projects	either	directly	or	through	joint ventures, beyond the limits prescribed by Navratna guidelines	of	DPE.	This	investment	is	also	exempt	from	the	₹1,000	crore	limit	in	a	single	entity	and	the	overall	ceiling	of	30%	of	net	worth	by	the	Cabinet	Committee	on	Economic	Affairs	(CCEA).
Record Capex Achievement
FY 2024-25 was a landmark year for NLC India Limited as the Company achieved its highest-ever capital expenditure of	₹7,736.10	crore,	exceeding	the	Ministry	of	Coal’s	target	of	₹3,040	crore.	This	reflects	not	just	the	scale	of	our	ambition but also our determination to accelerate projects that	are	central	to	our	long-term	growth	and	transformation.
Our investments during the year were strategically directed 
across mining, thermal, renewable energy and supporting infrastructure,	with	the	following	notable	progress:
Mining Expansion
Coal Production from Pachwara South OCP Mines is expected shortly ensuring fuel security to the linked GTPS	Power	Plant.	Development	of	Commercial	Coal	Mines	viz.	North	Dhadu	(Western	Part),	Machhakatta	(Revised), New Patrapara, strengthening our pathway towards	achieving	104.35	MTPA	mining	capacity	by	2030.	Your Company has also ventured into Critical Minerals Mining Business by bagging the Critical Minerals Block of Semhardih Phosphorite and Limestone Block and the Raipura	Phosphorite	and	Limestone	Block	at	Chhattisgarh.	These projects will ensure sustainable fuel security for our	expanding	generation	portfolio.Introduction
NLC India Limited

=== page 9 ===
Talabira II & III OCP
This	flagship	mine	has	scaled	up	strongly	to	its	production	
capacity of 20 MTPA, with average daily despatches of around	45,000	tonnes.	Work	on	the	dedicated	railway	siding	is	progressing	steadily.	The	introduction	of	Digital	Logistics Management System (DLMS) has optimised coal	dispatch	efficiency,	improving	turnaround	time	and	enhancing	transparency.
Acquisition of new commercial coal blocks these mining 
rights and project advancements are enabling us to align our	efforts	with	Vision	2030.	It	is	expected	to	provide	secure and sustainable fuel supply to existing and upcoming thermal projects, diversify our geographical footprint and resource base and strengthen operational resilience and	cost	competitiveness.	It	will	also	make	NLCIL	a	resource-secure and future-ready enterprise, supporting India’s	energy	security.
Machhakata (Revised) Coal Mine
The CMDPA was signed in July 2024, with the Vesting Order	issued	in	September	2024.	Geological	Report	approval was received in March 2025, and the Mining Plan along with the Mine Closure Plan has been submitted to the Ministry	of	Coal.	Land	acquisition	and	R&R	arrangements	are progressing with active support from the Government of Odisha, while railway connectivity is being developed through	RITES.	Once	operational,	Machhakata	will	substantially enhance our coal production capacity and fuel	security.
New Patrapara South Coal Mine
With CMDPA signed in December 2024 and Vesting Order issued in February 2025, this project has moved into	the	planning	stage.	The	Geological	Report	has	received approval, and the Mining Plan and Mine Closure Plan	are	under	preparation.	Targeted	for	commissioning	by	FY	2029-30,	the	mine	will	contribute	significantly	towards our long-term coal production and diversify our	supply	sources.
North Dhadu (Western Part) Coal Mine
The CMDPA was signed in September 2023, and in FY 2024-25, the Board approved the DPR and investment proposal	with	a	sanctioned	cost	of	₹1,354	crore.	Notifications	under	the	CBA	Act	have	been	issued,	and	railway	siding	development	is	advancing.Mine-III at Neyveli
The Mining Plan and Mine Closure Plan received approval from	the	Ministry	of	Coal	in	August	2024.	With	a	capacity	of	11.5	MTPA,	Mine-III	will	play	a	critical	role	in meeting fuel requirements for the upcoming TPS-II Second Expansion (1,000 MW), reinforcing our integrated mine-cum-power	model.
Diversification	into	Critical	Minerals
As	part	of	its	diversification	strategy,	your	Company	participated in the Tranche V auction of Critical and Strategic Mineral Blocks conducted by the Ministry of Mines, Government of India in May 2025, and was declared successful bidder for the Semhardih Phosphorite and Limestone Block and the Raipura Phosphorite and Limestone	Block,	both	located	in	Chhattisgarh.
Under the guidance of the Ministry of Coal and the 
Ministry of Mines, your Company is exploring possibilities for	acquiring	overseas	critical	minerals	assets.
Thermal Power Projects
A major milestone was the commissioning of Unit-I of Ghatampur Thermal Power Station (660 MW) in December	2024.	Unit	II	&	III	are	under	construction	and	will consolidate our position in the supercritical category, improving	efficiency	and	lowering	emissions.
Renewable Energy
The	year	saw	strong	momentum	in	our	renewable	projects:
• Barsingsar 300 MW Solar Project is progressing well and	scheduled	for	commissioning	by	December,	2025.
• The	first	phase	of	the	project	with	a	capacity	of	52.83	MW	has	been	successfully	commissioned.
• 150 MW Hybrid Wind-Solar Project is under development	at	Gujarat.
• 600 MW Solar Project at Khavda Solar Park, Gujarat
• 200 MW Solar Project under CPSU scheme in Gujarat is currently	under	implementation.
• Preliminary activities underway for the 810 MW Pugal Solar Park Project	in	Rajasthan.Infrastructure & Evacuation Systems
Your Company is implementing major works on railway sidings at Talabira, North Dhadu (Western Part), Pachwara South OCP and Machhakata, alongside deployment of digital	logistics	solutions.	The	works	are	advancing	rapidly	to	ensure	efficient	and	transparent	coal	evacuation.
Once commissioned, these assets will deliver long-term 
value by securing long-term fuel availability through expanded mining capacity generation and addition of substantial generation capacity across thermal and renewable	 energy.	It	is	also	expected	to	improve	operational	
efficiency	through	modern	infrastructure	and	digital	systems	and	strengthen	financial	performance	by	diversifying	revenue	streams.
Sustainability and Innovation
Sustainability is a core pillar of our growth strategy, deeply embedded	in	everything	we	do.	We	have	made	significant	progress in pioneering projects that support circular economy practices, clean energy integration and green technology	adoption.OB to M-Sand Initiative
As	a	“Waste	to	Wealth”	initiative,	in	a	first-of-its-kind	step	in the mining sector, NLCIL has converted Overburden (OB) material from its lignite mines into Manufactured Sand (M-Sand) to reduce the environmental footprint of its mining operations and provide a sustainable alternative to	river	sand.	At	Mine	I,	a	plant	with	a	capacity	of	1.0	MTPA	is	under	construction	and	approvals	from	the	Government of Tamil Nadu (GoTN) have been obtained for	M-Sand	production.	At	Mine	IA,	a	0.42	MTPA	plant has received CTO and GoTN approval, and sale agreements	are	being	finalised.
This initiative not only reduces waste but also addresses the 
acute shortage of construction-grade sand in Tamil Nadu, setting	an	example	of	circular	economy	in	action.
Lignite to Methanol Project
With	a	planned	capacity	of	0.40	MTPA	methanol	production, this project is envisaged as a strategic diversification	to	support	India’s	energy	security	and	clean	fuel	roadmap.	Although	the	revised	DPR	indicates	cost	escalation	and	financial	viability	challenges	due	to	existing methanol prices in the market, NLCIL continues to engage with stakeholders and evaluate options for future	development.	This	underlines	our	commitment	to	innovation	in	lignite-based	clean	fuel	technologies.

Green Hydrogen Pilot Plant
NLCIL is advancing a 4 MW Green Hydrogen pilot project 
at	Neyveli,	using	solar	power	as	the	input.	The	plant	will	have the capacity to produce 300 kg of hydrogen per day of	99.999%	purity	and	will	operate	during	sunshine	hours.	It	is	in	the	advanced	stage	of	procurement	of	electrolysers.	On commissioning, this will position NLCIL among the early movers in India’s green hydrogen economy, paving the	way	for	large-scale	adoption	in	future.
Renewable Energy in Mined-out and 
Industrial Areas (First of its kind in India)
To	maximise	land	use	efficiency,	NLCIL	is	establishing	
a	50	MW	solar	power	project	in	the	backfilled	area	of	Mine-II.	In	addition,	4	MW	rooftop	solar	and	1	MW	floating	solar	at	Neyveli	and	JV	companies	are	under	implementation.	These	projects	reinforce	our	philosophy	of aligning renewable capacity expansion with responsible land	management.
Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) 
and Pumped Storage
Through its subsidiary NIRL, NLCIL has won a 
250 MW/500 MWh Battery Energy Storage System project in Tamil Nadu and also pursuing for the same in other	States	as	well.	Further,	pumped	storage	projects	are	being pursued in Tamil Nadu and Odisha to strengthen grid	stability	and	renewable	energy	integration.Together,	these	initiatives	reflect	NLCIL’s	multipronged	approach to sustainability – recycling waste into resources, investing in clean fuels, decarbonising operations and enabling	renewable	energy	integration.	By	pursuing	such	forward-looking initiatives, NLCIL is not only contributing to India’s national goals of energy transition and circular economy but also positioning itself as a responsible, future-ready	enterprise	committed	to	sustainable	growth.
ESG & Safety
At	NLCIL,	safety	and	governance	are	integral	pillars.	We are implementing robust monitoring systems and employee training programmes aimed at achieving a ‘Zero	Harm’	workplace.	Our	ESG	roadmap	is	being	aligned	with	global	benchmarks	and	India’s	Net	Zero	2070	mission.
Inclusive Growth for Communities
Beyond	operational	and	financial	performance,	your Company remains deeply committed to inclusive development.	Our	CSR	efforts	have	impacted	thousands	of	lives	across	our	operational	geographies.	Initiatives	such as the establishment of STEM labs in schools, supporting healthcare camps, providing safe drinking water and empowering women and youth with livelihood opportunities are helping us make a meaningful difference	at	the	grassroots	level.We	are	equally	committed	to	environmental	stewardship.	Initiatives	such	as	large-scale	afforestation,	conversion	of	overburden into M-Sand, renewable energy deployment in mined-out areas and pioneering projects in green hydrogen and battery storage demonstrate our responsibility towards future	generations.
Going forward, one of our focus areas will be to further 
strengthen community participation by aligning skill development and livelihood programmes with the opportunities created by our expanding mining, power and renewable	energy	projects.	This	approach	will	not	only	uplift local communities but also create a stronger, more inclusive	ecosystem	for	sustainable	growth.
In essence, NLCIL’s journey is about powering the nation 
while	uplifting	lives.	We	are	proud	to	be	recognised	as	a	partner in progress, committed to inclusive development, environmental responsibility and creating long-term value for	all	stakeholders.
Looking Ahead
We	aspire	to	achieve	104.35	MTPA	mining	capacity,	more than 10 GW in thermal power capacity and 10 GW in renewable energy capacity by 2030 in alignment and contribution to GoI’s Energy Security and Clean Energy and continuous reduction in carbon intensity through supercritical	and	emerging	clean	technologies.
The coming year holds tremendous promise for NLC India 
Limited, as several of our major projects move towards commissioning	and	critical	milestones.
Commissioning of the remaining two units of Ghatampur 
Thermal Power Station (2 × 660 MW) will add 1,320 MW of supercritical capacity, enabling the station to achieve its	Commercial	Operation	Date	(CoD).	This	will	mark	a	quantum	jump	in	our	thermal	generation,	significantly	strengthening the Company’s baseload contribution to the national	grid.
In the renewable energy space, multiple projects are poised 
for	commissioning.Together, these renewable additions will meaningfully increase our clean energy footprint and reinforce NLCIL’s role	in	supporting	India’s	energy	transition.
Our upcoming projects such as Pachwara south, NUPPL, 
Machhakata (Revised), New Patrapara South, North Dhadu (Western Part) and Neyveli Mine III are expected to bring us	closer	to	our	objective	of	achieving	104.35	MTPA	mining capacity, ensuring secure and sustainable fuel supply	for	our	growing	generation	portfolio.
With	significant	capacity	additions,	renewable	energy	
integration and mining advancements, the Company is poised to embark on a strong growth trajectory, making way	for	a	bright	and	sustainable	future	for	all	stakeholders.
Acknowledgement
We have not only consolidated our position as a leading lignite	miner	and	power	producer	but	also	redefined	our	roadmap	to	become	a	future-ready	energy	enterprise.
I extend my sincere gratitude for the guidance and support 
extended	by	Ministry	of	Coal,	Government	of	India.	I	also	extend my deep appreciation to our employees, contract workmen, contractors, joint venture partners, Investors, Bankers, Central and State authorities and our valued shareholders	for	their	trust	and	support.	Together,	we	are	powering a brighter, more inclusive and sustainable future for	India.
Let us continue this journey with resolve, responsibility 
and	readiness	for	the	opportunities	that	lie	ahead	of	us.	With the unwavering support of all our stakeholders and the collective commitment of Team NLCIL, we step confidently	into	the	future—driving	sustainable	growth,	ensuring safety, embracing innovation, and creating enduring	value	for	our	great	nation.
Warm regards,
Prasanna Kumar Motupalli

Operational plantsNLCIL at a Glance
NLC India Limited (NLCIL), a distinguished Navratna enterprise of the Government of India, 
is committed towards addressing the nation’s energy needs through sustainable and responsible business	practices.	Established	in	1956,	the	Company	is	engaged	in	lignite/coal	mining	and	power	generation.	Over	the	years,	it	has	also	diversified	into	renewable	energy	and	coal	mining.	As a leading Central Public Sector Enterprise (CPSE), NLCIL plays a key role in meeting the electricity demands of multiple states, including Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala,	Telangana,	Rajasthan	and	the	Union	Territory	of	Puducherry	and	Andaman.	(MTPA) 
Mining capacity
69th Integrated Annual Report FY 2024-2516 NLC India Limited 17About the Company

Mines
NLCIL’s mining operations provide the essential fuel 
supply	for	its	integrated	power	business.	The	Company	operates four open-cast lignite mines at Neyveli (Mine I, Mine IA, and Mine II) and Barsingsar, along with the Talabira	II	&	III	coal	mines.	Lignite	from	Neyveli	and	Barsingsar is primarily supplied to the linked pit-head thermal power plants, while also meeting the requirements of independent power producers and other industrial consumers.	Coal	from	the	Talabira	mines	further	augments this capacity, supporting both NLCIL’s captive power	stations	and	external	customers.	Together,	these	operations	ensure	reliable,	cost-effective,	and	sustainable	fuel supply, strengthening NLCIL’s role in meeting the nation’s	energy	needs.Thermal Power Generation
Thermal power generation is a cornerstone of NLCIL’s business	model,	with	the	Company	running	five	thermal	power	stations	across	key	locations	in	India.	These	stations,	including those at Neyveli and Barsingsar, collectively contribute an installed thermal power generation capacity of	3,640	MW.	NLCIL	also	continues	to	expand	its	thermal	capacity with new projects such as the Neyveli New Thermal	Power	Project,	adding	1,000	MW	to	the	grid.	The Company’s thermal plants are critical for meeting the electricity demands of various states, driving industrial growth	and	enhancing	energy	security.	Through	its	thermal	operations, NLCIL ensures consistent and dependable supply	of	electricity,	significantly	contributing	to	the	nation’s	energy	infrastructure.Renewable Energy
As a pioneer in renewable energy, NLCIL has made	significant	strides	in	solar	and	wind	power	generation.	The	Company	has	installed	a	total	renewable	energy	capacity	of	1,483.89	MW,	including ground-mounted solar, rooftop solar, floating	solar	and	wind	power	projects.	NLCIL	was	the	first	Central	Public	Sector	Enterprise	to	surpass	1	GW	of	solar	capacity.	The	Company’s	renewable energy initiatives extend across the country, with notable projects in Neyveli and the	Andaman	Islands.	These	efforts	align	with	NLCIL’s	commitment	to	sustainability,	offering	cleaner energy solutions that help to reduce its carbon	footprint.	NLCIL’s	renewable	energy	capacity	not	only	fulfils	the	nation’s	power	demand	but also contributes to India’s commitment to meet	its	ambitious	renewable	energy	targets.
Marketing of Lignite, Coal and 
Minor Minerals
The marketing division of NLCIL handles the sale 
of raw lignite, coal and minor minerals such as ball	clay	and	silica	sand.	Raw	lignite	is	primarily	sourced from the Neyveli and Barsingsar mines and	sold	through	e-auction.	NLCIL	also	markets	coal from the Talabira mines, with e-auction sales beginning	in	2021.	Additionally,	the	Company	sells minor minerals and M-Sand to further diversify	its	portfolio.	2 GW
Renewable energy projects are under implementation in advance stage

Business Portfolio 
NLC India Limited (NLCIL) operates across a diverse range of sectors, primarily focused on mining, thermal 
power	generation,	renewable	energy	and	the	marketing	of	coal	and	raw	materials.	With	market	leadership	in	energy production and a commitment to sustainable practices, NLCIL plays a pivotal role in meeting the growing energy	demands	of	the	nation.	The	Company’s	operations	span	across	various	states	and	regions,	contributing	to	its	economic	growth	and	development.

Governance
Upholding our commitment to ethical and responsible business conduct, we strive to adhere to the highest 
standards	of	corporate	governance.	Our	governance	framework	is	built	on	values	such	as	transparency,	integrity,	accountability, inclusiveness and social responsibility, enabling us to consistently act in the best interests of all our	stakeholders.	These	values	are	not	just	part	of	our	operations	but	are	deeply	embedded	in	every	facet	of	our	decision-making	process,	reinforcing	our	dedication	to	ethical	conduct	and	sustainable	practices.
Our	approach	to	Environmental,	Social	and	Governance	(ESG)	principles	is	integral	to	our	operational	strategy.	
Through	continuous	engagement	with	stakeholders,	we	strive	to	ensure	that	our	governance	policies	are	a	reflection	of	an	evolving	industry	landscape.	We	strive	to	create	long-term	value	by	fostering	responsible	decision-making	and prioritising inclusivity in all our endeavours while adhering to rigorous governance standards that support sustainable 	growth.
Business Ethics and Standards
In line with our commitment to uphold ethical business 
practices, we consistently maintain fairness and integrity in all our engagements, with suppliers, contractors or bidders.	The	Integrity	Pact	Programme,	developed	in	collaboration with the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) and Transparency International India, demonstrates our	commitment	to	transparent	operations.	This	programme	mandates	that	all	tenders	exceeding	₹1	crore	include	an	Integrity Pact, ensuring a framework of accountability for	all	involved	parties.
Furthermore, we have established robust policies and 
procedures that apply universally to all stakeholders, including employees, vendors, suppliers, contractors and	the	Board	of	Directors.	These	guidelines	enable	us	to conduct business in an ethical manner and uphold the highest standards of integrity, fostering a culture of trust and aligning our activities with globally recognised best practices	in	corporate	governance.Anti-Corruption Processes and Practices
To safeguard the integrity of our operations, we have developed a comprehensive Personnel Manual that clearly outlines the responsibilities of our employees for upholding ethical standards and actively engaging in anti-corruption initiatives.	The	Code	of	Conduct	for	senior	management	and Board-level executives further ensures transparency and helps to uphold the highest standards of governance across	all	levels.
Our commitment extends beyond internal operations, 
encompassing our suppliers, contractors, joint ventures and	subsidiaries.	We	are	unwavering	in	our	adherence	to	anti-corruption regulations set by the Central Vigilance Commission,	which	apply	to	all	aspects	of	our	business.	By maintaining rigorous anti-bribery and anti-corruption policies, we ensure that ethical governance practices are embedded	in	every	facet	of	our	organisation.Vigilance
Our Vigilance Department plays an essential role in preserving the integrity of our operations by preventing corruption	and	misconduct.	This	department	is	integral	to upholding our anti-corruption policies, conducting vigilance workshops and raising awareness among our	employees.	Through	regular	preventive	vigilance	programmes, we create awareness among our people about the importance of maintaining high ethical standards and acting	in	compliance	with	the	Company’s	values.
In	addition	to	internal	efforts,	we	have	pioneered	initiatives	
such as the Ethical Forum in collaboration with Neyveli Schools	and	the	NTPL	project.	This	forum	is	designed	to	educate	the	younger	generation	about	the	significance	of ethical behaviour and vigilance, fostering a culture of integrity	and	responsibility	from	an	early	age.
Governance Structure
Our governance structure is led by the Board of Directors and is responsible for overseeing the Company’s corporate governance	framework.	Through	regular	meetings,	the	Board ensures that our governance practices adhere to the highest standards of transparency, accountability and ethical	conduct.
The Audit Committee, a critical sub-committee of the 
Board, plays an indispensable role in maintaining the integrity	of	our	financial	reporting	and	internal	control	systems.	The	committee’s	work	is	aligned	with	the	Companies Act, 2013, SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 and the DPE	Guidelines	on	Corporate	Governance.	While	there	may be occasional exceptions outlined in the Corporate Governance	Certificate	and	Secretarial	Audit	Report,	we	diligently comply with all governance requirements to promote	investor	confidence	and	trust.

Shri Prasanna Kumar Motupalli
Chairman and Managing Director (CMD) of NLCIL
Shri Prasanna Kumar Motupalli assumed charge of Chairman 
and Managing Director (CMD) of NLC India Limited (NLCIL)	on	January	12,	2023.	Prior	to	his	appointment, 	
he served as the Managing Director of Gujarat State Electricity	Corporation	Ltd.	(GSECL).
He had rich experience of more than three decades in the energy sector including power, Coal and also in heading Regulatory	bodies.	He	had	held	many	prestigious	positions 	
including Executive Director at NTPC (Corporate Fuel Management),	Director	of	CNUPL	(CIL	NTPC	Urja	Pvt. 	
Ltd.),	Joint	Managing	Director	of	MGCL	(MahaGuj	Collieries 	
Limited) and also served as the Chairman of the prestigious Western Region Power Committee (WRPC) and achieved remarkable	performance	even	during	challenging	times.
He hails from erstwhile Andhra Pradesh/Telangana and holds a gold medal in Mechanical Engineering from Andhra/Nagarjuna	University.	He	is	holding	MBA	in	four	specialisations,	viz.	Operation	Management,	Marketing	Management, Human Resource Management and Financial Management.	He	is	also	a	Certified	Energy	Auditor	from	the	Bureau	of	Energy	Efficiency,	GoI,	and	holds	the	prestigious	IPMA	Project	Director	(Level	A)	certification,	the pinnacle of global project management competency, recognising his exemplary leadership and proven ability to execute	complex	projects	at	the	strategic	level.	In	addition,	he	is	certified	in	Power	Distribution	Management,	further	strengthening	his	expertise	in	the	power	sector.
He is a fellow member of The Institution of Engineers (India), has presented and published numerous papers in prestigious National and International Conferences and Journals.	He	has	received	many	accolades,	including	the	Best Journal Award from The Institution of Engineers (India) and the ‘Horizon Best Article Award’ from NTPC Management Journal, including Bravery Award in NTPC for averting major accident in Singrauli Super Thermal Power	Plant	with	his	timely	courageous	efforts.  He has received applauds for his technical/leadership contributions from many reputed global institutions TUNRA, Australia, USAID, USA, IIM Ahmedabad, IIM	Lucknow	etc.
His expertise lies in power plant erection, operations and maintenance, Fuel management & handling, maintenance of heavy earth moving equipment, rolling stock operations and	maintenance,	Renewables,	and	all	green	initiatives.	He was instrumental in bringing National level policies in	energy	sector	that	helped	in	efficient	and	optimum	utilisation	of	different	fuels	in	generating	electricity	that	resulted	in	reduced	the	power	tariff.	During	his	tenure	as	MD, GSECL, excelled in Capacity Addition, operational excellence and safety through constant innovation and initiatives - received Outstanding Performance Appreciation	accolades	from	Govt.	of	Gujarat.
After his assumption of charge as CMD, NLCIL has 
ventured	into	first	time	RE	business	at	PAN	India	Level,	Commercial Mining and pioneering Critical Mineral Mining.	Currently	more	than	2	GW	RE	projects	are	under	implementation, 3 commercial coal blocks of 45 MTPA capacity won in competitive bidding conducted by Ministry of Coal, also won 2 Critical Mineral Blocks in competitive bidding conducted by Ministry of Mines and MOUs signed with	three	State	Governments	i.e.,	Assam,	Rajasthan	and	Maharashtra for setting up of 3 GW RE projects and also putting	Thermal	power	Projects.	Company	has	diversified	its operations into wealth from waste including extraction M-Sand from Mine Overburden, putting up of RE projects in	mined	out	lands.	Successfully	carried	diversion	of	Paravanar river including taking possession of more than 500 Ha of acquired land in Neyveli mines which is pending more	than	a	decade.	Instrumental	in	awarding	much	awaited	EPC	contract	for	the	pit-head	green	field	Talabira	Ultra Super critical Thermal Project of 3x800 MW and also overcoming challenges accomplished the commissioning of the much awaited 1st super critical thermal unit 1 (660	MW)	at	Ghatampur	Thermal	Project	in	Uttar	Pradesh.	He ensured all round performance improvement of the Company in all fronts including building Stakeholders confidence	and	enhancing	the	market	capitalisation	to	multi	fold.	The	above	developments	have	laid	a	strong	foundation	for	realising	NLCIL’s	ambitious	Vision	2030	targets:	doubling thermal and mining capacities, and achieving a	multifold	increase	in	renewable	energy	capacity.	Specifically,	the	company	is	on	track	to	reach	10	GW	of	thermal	capacity,	10.1	GW	of	renewable	energy	capacity,	and	over	100	MTPA	in	mining	capacity	by	2030.
He has been honoured with many prestigious awards, 
including ‘Top Rankers Excellence - CEO of the year’ for 2025, ‘People-Focused CEO of the Year’ award by ET Human Capital Awards 2024, Prestigious Dr.	Yalavarthy	Nayudamma	Memorial	Award	for	2024	for his contributions in science, technology and societal development and best CEO Corporate Management innovative	leadership	award	2023.

Board Committees
Our Company has established 17 Board committees for supporting the Board of Directors in executing its responsibilities 
with	efficiency	and	precision.	These	committees	act	as	key	enablers	in	delegating	critical	tasks	to	operational	teams,	facilitating	a	streamlined	decision-making	process	that	aligns	with	the	company’s	strategic	goals.
It	also	makes	the	governance	framework	effective	and	transparent.	It	promotes	accountability	and	sound	decision-making	
across	all	levels	of	the	organisation.	By	overseeing	critical	areas	such	as	Finance,	Audit,	Risk	Management,	Corporate	Social Responsibility (CSR) and Governance, these committees provide valuable insights and actively contribute to shaping the	strategic	direction	of	NLCIL.	The	combined	efforts	of	the	Board	and	its	committees	enable	the	Company	to	remain	focused	on	its	long-term	growth	objectives	while	safeguarding	the	interests	of	all	stakeholders.	Governance

Stakeholder Management
We	consider	continuous	communication	with	stakeholders	essential	for	fostering	sustained	growth.	Regular	
engagement with stakeholders provides us with valuable insights into their expectations and concerns, allowing us	to	strategically	allocate	resources	to	areas	that	will	generate	the	maximum	impact.	By	aligning	our	business	processes with the diverse needs of our stakeholders, we ensure that our actions not only create value for them but	also	contribute	to	the	long-term	sustainability	of	NLCIL.	Effective	dialogue	with	stakeholders	strengthens	relationships,	enhances	transparency	and	empowers	us	to	be	responsive	and	responsible.
Our	engagement	strategy	is	structured	around	understanding	the	unique	concerns	of	each	stakeholder	group.	We	engage	
with	our	employees	to	foster	a	safe	and	inclusive	workplace	that	supports	their	professional	development.	For	suppliers	and	customers,	we	maintain	strong	partnerships	that	focus	on	sustainable	procurement	practices,	innovation	and	efficiency.	We also undertake targeted CSR initiatives for addressing socio-economic needs and facilitating the holistic development of	communities.	Consequently,	we	collaborate	with	regulatory	authorities	to	ensure	compliance	and	contribute	to	public	policy	development. Materiality Assessment
As part of our commitment to transparent and accountable sustainability practices, NLCIL conducted a 
comprehensive	materiality	assessment	through	a	structured	four-step	process.	This	approach	allowed	us	to	systematically 	identify	and	prioritise	material	topics	that	were	most	relevant	to	our	business	and	stakeholders. 	
The	outcome	of	this	process	reflects	the	issues	that	significantly	influence	operational	resilience,	long-term	performance	and	stakeholder	trust.
In line with our ongoing commitment to ESG integration, 
we revisited the existing material topics during the current reporting	cycle.	This	review	was	undertaken	to	evaluate	the need for incorporating any new or emerging areas of	concern.	As	a	result,	we	acknowledged	the	growing	importance of Freedom of Association and Collective Bargaining and Economic Impacts, both of which are addressed	in	this	report.
While the current list of material topics remains 
unchanged, we continue to focus on the most impactful areas	that	drive	business	value	and	sustainability	outcomes.	These insights reinforce our proactive and responsive approach to materiality, ensuring that we stay aligned with evolving expectations, ESG standards and long-term corporate	objectives.

Approach for Management
At NLCIL, we rely heavily on natural resources, including 
lignite	and	coal,	for	our	operations.	We	manage	resource	availability by adopting cutting-edge technologies that enhance	resource	efficiency.	Through	the	use	of	modern	mining equipment and process optimisation strategies, we minimise environmental impacts while maximising the output of our resources, thereby ensuring long-term environmental	sustainability.	We	also	explore	new	technologies to minimise resource consumption and improve	overall	efficiency	of	our	operations,	thereby	reducing	dependence	on	non-renewable	resources.
Approach for Management
Our operations, including excavation, drilling and coal transport, result in air emissions, particularly particulate matter and CO
2.	To	manage	this,	we	employ	technologies	
like sprinkler and fog systems, greenbelt development, and Flue	Gas	Desulphurisation	(FGD)	systems.	We	actively	reduce emissions by implementing dust suppression methods in high-risk areas such as coal stockyards and roadways	within	mines.	These	measures	minimise	the	negative environmental impacts of our operations and ensure compliance with air quality regulations, supporting the long-term sustainability of our business while protecting	air	quality.
Approach for Management
We address water management by employing state-of-the-art	sewage	treatment	plants	(STPs)	and	effluent	treatment	plants (ETPs) that recycle water for reuse in greenbelt development.	Additionally,	we	implement	rainwater	harvesting	and	artificial	recharge	techniques	to	replenish	groundwater	levels.	Our	efforts	minimise	the	depletion	of	local water sources and help maintain sustainable water use	across	our	operations.	We	continuously	monitor	water quality and implement corrective measures to limit negative	impact	on	communities	or	ecosystems.Resource Availability

Risk Management  
At NLC India Limited, we recognise that the scale and complexity of our operations inevitably expose us to a wide 
spectrum	of	risks.	These	risks	range	from	geological	and	environmental	uncertainties	in	mining,	to	volatility	in	global	energy	markets,	regulatory	changes	in	the	power	sector,	and	the	growing	imperatives	of	climate	transition.	We are acutely aware that the manner in which we anticipate and address such challenges determines not only the stability	of	our	operations	but	also	the	confidence	of	our	stakeholders	and	the	sustainability	of	our	growth.
For	us,	risk	management	is	not	a	peripheral	exercise,	but	an	intrinsic	part	of	our	strategy.	By	embedding	robust	
governance mechanisms, rigorous controls, and continuous oversight, we ensure that risks are systematically identified,	evaluated,	and	mitigated—while	also	creating	space	to	seize	emerging	opportunities	in	the	evolving	energy	landscape	of	India.
Strategic Risk Governance
Our	governance	framework	for	risk	management	is	firmly	
aligned with internationally recognised standards such as	the	COSO	Integrated	Framework	and	ISO	31000:2018	guidelines.	This	ensures	that	our	practices	are	benchmarked	against global best practice, while remaining sensitive to the distinct realities of the mining and energy sectors in which	we	operate.	Oversight	is	exercised	through	the	Risk	Management Committee of the Board, which provides strategic direction and ensures that risk deliberations are integrated	into	the	highest	levels	of	decision-making.Operational Control and Compliance
Given the scale of our mining operations and power projects, we have instituted rigorous internal controls that extend across contracts, procurement, project execution,	and	human	resources.	Authorised	manuals	and process frameworks govern each of these domains, ensuring	consistency,	compliance,	and	accountability.	By maintaining clarity of procedure, we reduce the scope for operational and compliance lapses and create resilience in the day-to-day functioning of our business units	across	India.
Independent Audit and Assurance
We place strong emphasis on transparency and independent evaluation.	Leading	Chartered	Accountants	firms	are	engaged to conduct comprehensive audits across all our mines,	thermal	stations,	and	renewable	energy	sites.	These	reviews	not	only	validate	the	reliability	of	our	financial	and operational systems but also provide critical external insights	that	strengthen	our	internal	controls.	Audit	outcomes are subject to rigorous scrutiny by the Audit Committee, which works in close consultation with both internal and statutory auditors to ensure that any emerging risks	are	addressed	promptly	and	decisively.
Proactive Risk Culture and 
Capacity Building
Our employees undergo regular training on risk awareness 
and control, tailored to the unique challenges of mining operations, power plant management, and renewable project execution.	Quarterly	risk	evaluations	are	carried	out	by	the Internal Risk Review Committee, with subsequent reviews by the Board-level Risk Management Committee and	the	Audit	Committee.	This	cycle	of	evaluation,	review,	and	refinement	enables	us	to	remain	agile	in	responding	to	shifting market conditions, environmental obligations, and technological 	disruptions.Commitment to Sustainable Value Creation
By institutionalising risk management across every layer of our business, we demonstrate our commitment to responsible	corporate	stewardship.	Our	framework	not	only safeguards our assets and reputation but also ensures that	we	remain	resilient	in	an	era	of	energy	transition.	Whether navigating the operational risks of large-scale lignite mining, the regulatory scrutiny of thermal power generation, or the execution challenges of scaling solar and wind capacity, we remain steadfast in aligning risk management with our mission of delivering sustainable, affordable,	and	reliable	energy	for	the	nation.
Risk	Identification	and	Evaluation
At	NLC	India	Limited,	we	approach	risk	identification	as	a	continuous	and	disciplined	exercise.	Through	our	dedicated	Corporate Risk Cell, we systematically gather inputs from across our mining, power generation, and renewable energy	operations.	These	inputs	are	consolidated	into	a	
Board of Directors
Audit Committee
Risk Management Committee
Director (Projects & Planning)
Risk Cell, Chief Risk Officer, Risk Controller
Unit Level Risk Owner & Risk ManagerInternal Risk Review Committee
(One member nominated from each of the 
Functional Directorates)comprehensive risk register, which serves as the central repository	of	potential	exposures	facing	the	organisation.	The register is not static; it is periodically reviewed and refined	under	the	guidance	of	the	Risk	Management	Committee (RMC), ensuring that strategic decisions at the highest level are fully informed by an up-to-date assessment	of	our	risk	environment.
For greater clarity and precision, we classify risks 
under three broad categories—Strategic, Business, and Operational.	This	framework	enables	us	to	differentiate	between long-term structural risks, such as energy transition imperatives or regulatory shifts, and operational risks that emerge from day-to-day mining, plant operations, or	supply	chain	dynamics.	Once	identified,	each	risk	is	assessed through both qualitative and quantitative lenses, capturing	its	potential	impact	and	likelihood	of	occurrence.	This dual-layered analysis empowers us to focus on risks with the greatest potential to disrupt performance or hinder sustainable 	growth.

Risk Prioritisation and Response
Following careful evaluation, we undertake a rigorous prioritisation process to ensure that our resources and oversight are 
allocated	where	they	are	most	needed.	Risks	with	higher	probability	and	severity	are	elevated	for	closer	scrutiny,	while	those	with	reduced	impact	are	monitored	with	proportionate	intensity.	Our	approach	distinguishes	between:Risk Management 
Risk Mitigation Strategy
At	NLC	India	Limited,	we	approach	risk	mitigation	as	a	strategic	enabler	of	sustainable	growth.	Our	framework	recognises 	
three	broad	categories	of	risk—Strategic,	Operational,	and	Business—and	embeds	tailored	responses	for	each.	By	combining 	
rigorous planning, technological innovation, and proactive engagement with stakeholders, we safeguard the continuity of our operations	while	positioning	the	Company	to	capture	new	opportunities	in	India’s	evolving	energy	landscape.
Land Acquisition and Availability
Land acquisition for large-scale mining and power	projects	continues	to	pose	significant	risks	due	to	diverse	ownership	patterns,	state-specific	legal frameworks, and sensitivities surrounding compensation	and	rehabilitation.	These	complexities	often lead to delays, which can adversely impact project timelines, expansion strategies, and cost efficiencies.
Renewable Energy Tariffs and 
Regulatory Delays
Preferential	tariff	schemes	from	regulators	such	
as	TNERC	carry	strict	commissioning	deadlines.	Delays	risk	the	forfeiture	of	tariff	benefits	and	unrecovered	dues	efficiencies.
Safety in Operations
Given the hazardous nature of mining and thermal power	generation,	worker	safety	is	a	critical	concern.	Any lapse can result in injury, production loss, and reputational	damage.Strategic Risks
Operational RisksNLCIL mitigates this risk through a multi-state, tailored 
approach aligned with the RFCTLARR Act, 2013 and the	CBA	Act,	1957,	while	adopting	state-specific	R&R	policies	to	address	local	socio-economic	needs.	We	engage proactively with district administrations, state governments, public representatives, and communities to ensure fair and transparent compensation, livelihood restoration,	and	resettlement	measures.	Leveraging	digital land management tools, grievance redressal mechanisms, and Board-level oversight, we balance stakeholder interests with project imperatives, thereby enabling timely land access and reinforcing long-term community	trust.
We pursue a dual approach—legal recourse where 
entitlements are at stake, and strengthened project execution frameworks that emphasise timely clearances, dedicated	SPVs,	and	close	engagement	with	regulators.

Driving Innovation and Sustainability
We recognise the crucial role that innovation and 
sustainability play in shaping the future of the energy sector.	With	efforts	to	allocate	capital	for	developing	clean	energy solutions, we are contributing to a sustainable future.	In	FY	2024-25,	we	undertook	the	following	initiatives	in	this	area:
• Renewable	Energy	Investment:	We	have	made	substantial	investments in expanding our renewable energy capacity, including solar and wind energy projects, which contribute to diversifying our energy portfolio and achieving carbon reduction	targets.
• Exploring	Green	Hydrogen:	As	part	of	our	forward-thinking strategy, we are expanding into emerging technologies like green hydrogen, which hold the potential to	redefine	energy	systems	and	offer	sustainable	solutions	for	the	future.
• Collaborative	Innovation:	We	continue	to	collaborate	with	industry leaders, academic institutions and government bodies to foster cutting-edge research and implement technologies that support our vision of a sustainable, low-carbon	economy.Ensuring	Operational	Efficiency 
and Capacity Building
Our focus on operational excellence ensures that every 
resource	is	utilised	effectively	to	drive	growth	while	minimising	waste	and	environmental	impact.	We	are	committed to improving the operational performance of all our divisions through targeted investments for improving efficiency.	
• Advanced	Mining	Practices:	We	have	adopted	latest	mining technologies to optimise extraction processes and minimise the environmental footprint of our operations, ensuring	sustainable	and	efficient	resource	management.
• Lignite	Resource	Optimisation:	Significant	investments	in R&D have been directed to improve lignite extraction methods	and	enhance	the	quality	of	resources.	It	plays	a	vital	role	in	maintaining	the	long-term	profitability	of	our	mining	operations.
• Capital	Efficiency:	We	are	focused	on	optimising	our	working capital and operational processes, leveraging technology	to	streamline	cash	flow	management	and	ensure	effective	allocation	of	resources.

55.8/100 59/100ESG Rating Outlook
NLC India Limited (NLCIL) considers the receipt of independent ESG ratings an important step in reinforcing its	commitment	to	sustainable	growth.	These	benchmarks	provide transparency, guide long-term strategy, and strengthen	stakeholder	confidence	in	the	Company’s	environmental,	social,	and	governance	performance.
CareEdge	ESG	Ratings	awarded	NLCIL	a	score	of	55.8,	
the	first	ESG	rating	for	a	power-sector	entity	under	its	framework.	This	evaluation,	based	on	over	300	indicators	across	18	themes,	recognises	NLCIL’s	efforts	to	address	sector-specific	environmental	challenges	while	building	sustainable	practices.
ICRA ESG assigned a combined score of 59 (Adequate),

Mining and Production Capacity Overview 
We	operate	three	opencast	lignite	mines	at	Neyveli,	Tamil	Nadu,	with	a	combined	capacity	of	28.0	MTPA,	and	one	lignite	
mine	at	Barsingsar,	Rajasthan	with	2.10	MTPA,	yielding	a	total	lignite	mining	capacity	of	30.10	MTPA.	In	addition,	our	coal	mining	operations	at	Talabira	II	&	III	in	Odisha	contribute	20.0	MTPA,	bringing	our	overall	mining	capacity	to	50.10	MTPA.	This	robust	infrastructure	ensures	consistent	fuel	supply	to	our	thermal	power	plants,	enabling	us	to	integrate	our	mining	operations	with	power	generation	to	deliver	operational	resilience	and	continuity	in	energy	supply.30.10	MTPA

Capacity Expansion and Strategic Direction
We aim to enhance our total mining capacity to 104.35	MTPA	by	FY	2029-30,	supported	by	planned	investments	of	around	₹14,199	crore.	To	deliver	this,	NLCIL	has secured major coal assets including Machhakata (Revised), Angul, Odisha (30 MTPA), North Dhadu (Western Part), Latehar, Jharkhand (3 MTPA), and New Patrapara South, Angul, Odisha (12 MTPA), strengthening long-term	fuel	security	for	our	power	portfolio.	In	parallel,	to diversify into critical minerals, NLCIL has been declared preferred bidder for the Semhardih and Raipura phosphorite–limestone blocks in Balod, Chhattisgarh under the Ministry of Mines’ Tranche-V auction during May 2025, positioning the company to support domestic fertiliser and strategic	mineral	supply	chains.	We	aim	to	expand	thermal	power generation capacity from the present 5,300 MW to 10,020	MW	by	FY	2029-30.	It	is	anticipated	to	bolster	our	power generation capacity and enable us to undertake  joint venture projects like the 1,980 MW Ghatampur plant and establish lignite-based projects in Neyveli and coal-based projects	in	Odisha	in	future.
Mining Asset Utilisation and Sustainability
We utilise advanced extraction techniques in our mining operations and it enhances asset utilisation while limiting our	environmental	impact.	The	majority	of	our	lignite-fired	thermal power plants are pit-head units, allowing direct and	cost-effective	fuel	supply,	which	reinforces	operational	efficiency	and	reduces	logistics	risks.	By	integrating	mining	and power-generation assets, we maintain continuity of supply and ensure low fuel-related risks, primarily due to our ability to make captive fuel arrangements and long-term	fuel	linkages.Performance Review

Thermal Power Generation Overview 
We operate a total of 3,640 MW of lignite -based pithead 
thermal power capacity—comprising TPS -I Expn, TPS -II, 
TPS-II Expansion and NNTPS in Neyveli, Tamil Nadu, 
Barsingsar plant in Rajasthan, 1,000 MW coal- based 
thermal plant via our joint venture, NTPL in Tamil Nadu, 
and 660 MW capacity at our joint venture, NUPPL Ghatampur Thermal Power Project in Ghatampur, Uttar Pradesh collectively providing 5,300 MW of operational thermal	generation	capacity.
Enhancing Efficiency through Asset Integration
Our lignite power plants are located near captive lignite mines,	enabling	seamless	fuel	supply	and	cost-effective	operations—factors	that	significantly	reduce	logistic	exposure	and	enhance	plant	reliability.	Meanwhile,	NTPL	benefits	from	secure	fuel	arrangements	with	long-term	supply agreements and strategic coal supply partnerships, strengthening	its	operational	stability	and	financial	predictability.
Strategic Capacity Expansion and Modernisation
In December 2024, our joint venture, NUPPL commissioned the	first	660	MW	unit	of	the	1,980	MW	Ghatampur	plant, 	
an advanced coal -based installation featuring Selective 
Catalytic Reduction (SCR), Flue Gas Desulphurisation (FGD),	and	Zero	Liquid	Discharge	(ZLD)	systems. 	
The remaining units are expected to be commissioned by the	end	of	FY	2025-26.	This	reinforces	our	commitment 	
to cleaner thermal operations that can pave the path for a sustainable	future.
Renewable Energy Overview
We have steadily expanded our renewable energy footprint, reaching a total installed capacity of 1,483.89	MW,	of	which	1,432.89	MW	is	from	solar	and 	
51	MW	from	wind	sources.	Our	operations	include 	
grid-connected solar projects across Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh and Andaman, with notable initiatives such as the 20 MW (AC) Solar PV Plant integrated with 8 MWh Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) in Port Blair, commissioned under the Ministry of	New	and	Renewable	Energy’s	VGF	scheme.
Integrated Deployment and Innovation
The development of the Port Blair solar plant with BESS represents a key milestone in hybrid renewable technology	deployment.	This	project	not	only 	
supports reliable energy access for remote island grids but also showcases our capabilities in integrating advanced storage technologies with solar generation—critical for addressing intermittency and enabling a	stable	supply	profile.
Advanced Mine Planning and Design
For mine planning and design, we use advanced software such	as	AutoCAD	and	Surpac	to	ensure	efficiency	and	safe	mining	activities.
Scientific Studies and Slope Stability
We	have	conducted	scientific	studies	under	Regulation	106(2) of CMR, 2017 to assess slope stability across all mines,	with	full	implementation	of	the	recommendations.	Slope stability is also monitored using Total Station technology	for	accuracy	and	safety.
Training and Skill Development
We operate a well-equipped GVTC for training in line with MVTR	1966.	Our	VTC	includes	state-of-the-art	simulators	to train operators of SME, dozers, backhoes, and pipe layers.
Safety Systems and Protocols
We strictly ensure the use of the Lock-Out and Tag-Out (LOTO)	system.	All	safety	devices	fitted	in	equipment	and	HEMM	deployed	in	our	mines	comply	with	DGMS	(Tech.)	Circular	06	of	2020.	The	features	include:
• Automatic Fire Detection and Suppression System (AFDSS)
• Rear vision cameras
• Seat belts with reminders
• Reverse AVA systems
• Rear view mirrors
• Tramming alarms
• Turbo charger guards
• Fatigue sensors
Dust Suppression and Air Quality
To minimise hazards from coal dust, we have implemented robust dust suppression systems. At present, 30 water sprinklers and 3 fog cannons are deployed across NLCIL	mines.
Technology-enabled Mine Safety
We have introduced several technology-driven safety measures,	including:
• RFID barriers, CCTV surveillance, and geo-fencing
• Mine illumination levels maintained as per Regulation 178 of CMR, 2017 read with GSR 981(E) of 01/10/2018
• Wireless walkie-talkies  for reliable communication
Digital Safety Initiatives
On National Safety Day 2025, we launched the NLCIL 
Aran Mobile Safety App for reporting unsafe observations and near misses, enabling timely compliance and corrective	action.Vision 2030: Scaling Up for Impact
Our long-term renewable energy vision is firmly aligned with the Government of India’s green transition goals.	We	aim	to	increase	our	renewable	capacity 	
from	1.43	GW	to	10.11	GW	by	FY	2030,	a	sevenfold 	
expansion.	This	growth	will	be	driven	by	large-scale 	
solar parks, floating solar installations, and hybrid (solar–wind)	ventures	across	multiple	states.	To	execute 	
this transition, we are actively pursuing strategic partnerships, policy -linked incentives and land 
acquisition	in	high -solar-radiation	zones.
Enabling Decarbonisation through Diversification
Growth in our renewable energy portfolio complements our integrated business model, supporting our efforts for emission reduction and ensuring resilient power supply	in	the	long-term.	Through	NLC	India	Renewables 	
Ltd.	we	are	embedding	renewable	energy	development 	
into	our	core	operations.	Our	commitment	to	clean 	
energy is not merely a compliance measure, but a strategic	enabler	of	sustainable	value	creation.	It	is 	
also pivotal for reducing our carbon footprint and contributing	to	global	climate	action	goals.
Mine Safety and Operational Excellence
Blast-free Mining Practices
We practice blast-free lignite mining across all Neyveli mines using state-of-the-art technology such as bucket wheel	excavators,	belt	conveyors	and	spreaders.	Blast-free	mining is also implemented at Barsingsar mines for both overburden (OB) and lignite using conventional mining equipment.	At	Talabira	Mines,	coal	is	extracted	without	blasting	through	the	use	of	surface	miners.

Centre for Applied Research & Development (CARD)
The Centre for Applied Research & Development (CARD) is NLCIL’s in-house research and development unit, which 
has	been	a	cornerstone	of	innovation	since	its	inception.	Established	in	1958	as	the	Central	Laboratory,	it	was	recognised	by	the	Department	of	Science	&	Technology	in	1975.	In	1983,	it	was	renamed	to	its	current	designation,	CARD,	and	has	since	been	at	the	forefront	of	driving	technological	advancements	and	operational	efficiencies	within	NLCIL.	CARD’s	core	mission is to focus on research and development that aligns with the Company’s strategic goals of sustainability, operational excellence	and	technological	leadership.

Innovation Incubation Centre (IIC) 
at CARD
In FY 2024-25, NLCIL’s Centre for Applied Research 
and Development (CARD) introduced several digital innovations, with a primary focus on process automation and	operational	monitoring.	Real-time	monitoring	of	environmental parameters and quality control has been seamlessly	integrated	into	routine	testing	workflows	to	significantly	enhance	operational	efficiency	and	accuracy.	Alongside this, the Innovation Incubation Centre (IIC) at CARD, in collaboration with IISc Bangalore and Anna University, continues to focus on cutting-edge projects across	energy,	environment	and	healthcare.	Noteworthy	initiatives include smart IoT-based aeroponic herbal cultivation, membrane-less chemical-free wastewater treatment,	hydroponics	in	backfilled	mine	areas	and	the	development of geopolymer green bricks using solar heating.	Several	of	these	projects	have	progressed	from	proof of concept to prototype stages during FY 2024-25, reinforcing NLCIL’s role as an innovator in energy and environmental 	sectors.Driving Innovation and Sustainability
We recognise the crucial role that innovation and sustainability play in shaping the future of the energy sector.	With	efforts	to	allocate	capital	for	developing	clean	energy solutions, we are contributing to a sustainable future.	In	FY	2024-25,	we	undertook	the	following	initiatives	in	this	area:
• Renewable	Energy	Investment:	We	have	made	substantial	investments in expanding our renewable energy capacity, including solar and wind energy projects, which contribute to diversifying our energy portfolio and achieving carbon reduction	targets.
• Exploring	Green	Hydrogen:	As	part	of	our	forward-thinking strategy, we are expanding into emerging technologies like green hydrogen, which hold	the	potential	to	redefine	energy	systems	and	offer	sustainable	solutions	for	the	future.
• Collaborative	Innovation:	We	continue	to	collaborate	with	industry leaders, academic institutions and government bodies to foster cutting-edge research and implement technologies that support our vision of a sustainable, low-carbon	economy.Development of Eco-friendly Geo-polymer 
Ash-Based Green Bricks using Solar Heating
This project focuses on producing eco-friendly 
geo-polymer	bricks	from	fly	ash,	a	byproduct	of	thermal	
power stations, which are cured using solar heating instead	of	traditional	kiln	firing.	This	innovation	significantly	reduces	energy	consumption	and	carbon	emissions.	By	utilising	fly	ash,	the	process	also	promotes	the	reuse	of	waste	material.	Geo-polymer	bricks	offer	a sustainable alternative to conventional building material, thereby reducing the carbon footprint of the	construction	industry.
Key Collaborations at NLCIL
NLCIL	has	fostered	significant	collaborations	with	leading	institutions	to	strengthen	its	R&D	efforts.
Key Partnerships
• NIT Trichy and IISc Bangalore: Focused on enhancing the life of bottom rollers for mining equipment.
• IIT Madras:  Exploring semiconductor applications using lignite and humic acid.
• BARC: The Company signed a landmark Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Bhabha Atomic 
Research Centre (BARC) on 06th August, 2025 for a pioneering project to extract Rare Earth Elements (REEs) 
from fly ash.
Activated Carbon Development using Lignite – 
HA Sludge
This project aims to convert lignite and Humic Acid (HA) 
sludge into activated carbon, a high-demand material used	for	water	and	air	purification.	By	repurposing	carbon-rich sludge from lignite processing, it helps to reduce waste and produce activated carbon, known for its	excellent	adsorption	properties.	This	process	not	only	contributes	to	efficient	pollution	control	but	also	offers	a	sustainable,	cost-effective	method	for	producing	activated	carbon.	The	project	further	advances	waste	management	practices while promoting resource conservation and environmental	sustainability.Intellectual CapitalPerformance Review

Neyon – The Lion Mascot of NLC India Limited
NLC India Limited has always sought symbols that embody its strength, 
vision,	and	commitment	to	the	nation.	In	this	spirit,	the	lion	was	chosen	as the Company’s mascot, as it has long stood as one of the most enduring emblems	of	power	and	pride	in	India’s	history.
The lion is not new to India—it has always been an integral part of the 
nation’s	identity.	For	NLCIL,	the	lion	represents	courage	in	pioneering	energy solutions, leadership in the Indian power sector, stability in delivering	consistent	progress	and	pride	in	our	people,	planet	and	purpose.
To give this powerful symbol a distinct identity, the lion mascot was 
named ‘Neyon’—a blend of Neyveli, the birthplace of NLCIL, and lion, the	timeless	leader.	This	unique	name	links	the	Company’s	glorious	past	with	its	sustainable	future,	embodying	both	heritage	and	aspirations.	Neyon has since been featured prominently in several of NLCIL’s key campaigns, reinforcing its role as a unifying symbol of the Company’s journey	and	values.

Partnerships that Multiply Impact
In NLCIL’s view, meaningful partnerships catalyse 
community development by enhancing both its scale and the	pace	of	delivery.	During	FY	2024-25,	we	expanded	and deepened our collaborations with a diverse array of stakeholders, including DRDA Cuddalore, the National Power Training Institute (NPTI), ALIMCO, ROTI Foundation, Aravinda Charitable Society, and Neyam Veterinary	Welfare	Trust—among	others.	These	alliances	have empowered us to deliver projects more swiftly and extend our outreach in underserved regions, ensuring tangible,	long-term	benefits.
For example, our collaboration with DRDA Cuddalore 
expedited the delivery of vital infrastructure—such as community buildings and sanitation facilities—in local villages that would otherwise have faced lengthy delays	under	conventional	implementation	models.	Through NPTI, we facilitated targeted education interventions, supporting job-oriented diploma and postgraduate	programmes	specifically	designed	for	dependents	of	land	acquisition	beneficiaries	and	other	project-affected	persons,	thus	reinforcing	livelihoods	and	opportunities	for	upward	mobility.
Working	alongside	ALIMCO,	we	provided	artificial	limbs	
and assistive devices to Divyangjans across Cuddalore, Barsingsar, and Talabira—vastly improving the mobility, dignity	and	quality	of	life	of	beneficiaries	through	inclusive	support	mechanisms.	Additionally,	through	our partnership with ROTI Foundation, we supported nutritional outreach programmes for vulnerable communities, while collaboration with the Aravinda Charitable Society aided in the provision of healthcare and rehabilitation	services	for	marginalised	groups.	Similarly,	our engagement with the Neyam Veterinary Welfare Trust enhanced livestock healthcare and community resilience, recognising the symbiotic relationship between	animal	welfare	and	rural	livelihoods.
Beyond direct service delivery, these relationships have 
bolstered NLCIL’s reputation as a responsive and trusted public	sector	enterprise,	guided	by	efficiency,	empathy,	and	social	commitment.	Through	regular	evaluations	and	outcome monitoring—guided by frameworks such as the OECD DAC—we ensure that our CSR endeavours not only reach but genuinely enrich the lives of communities, aligning	corporate	responsibility	with	inclusive	growth.
Empowering through Education
Education	remains	a	cornerstone	of	our	social	investments.	In FY 2024-25, we supported the development of educational infrastructure at institutions such as Annamalai University, Saraswathi Shishu Vidya Mandir (Balimela), and	government	schools	in	Swaroopdesar	and	Marungur.	Under the Beti Padhao initiative, school kits were distributed	to	first-generation	girl	students,	while	Virtual	Reality Laboratories were introduced in government schools	to	strengthen	science	and	technology	learning.
We also reimbursed tuition fees for SC/ST and OBC 
students at Jawahar Science College, supported Kendriya Vidyalaya in Neyveli, and organised awareness and guidance	programmes	for	students,	parents,	and	teachers.	These initiatives collectively aim to improve access, quality, and equity in education, especially for underprivileged and marginalised	groups.
Elevating Community Health & Well-Being 
through Strategic Partnerships
At NLCIL, our commitment to community health 
transcends traditional models of care delivery, embracing sustained partnerships and infrastructure development to	deliver	measurable,	long-term	wellness	benefits.	In FY 2024-25, we deepened our strategic collaborations with organisations such as ALIMCO, DRDA Cuddalore, CHILDS Trust Hospital, and the NLCIL General Hospital, reinforcing a holistic and inclusive approach to healthcare in our	regions	of	operation.
Our NLCIL General Hospital in Neyveli continues to stand 
at the forefront of primary healthcare delivery, providing residents of surrounding villages with free medical consultations, routine diagnostic services, and occupational health	support—benefitting	a	significant	portion	of	the	local	population.	The	Medical	Branch	meticulously	monitors	services	offered	to	both	employee	families	and non-employee residents, ensuring that healthcare accessibility	remains	consistent	and	equitable.
Infrastructure investment forms a vital axis of our health 
strategy.	For	example,	at	the	Government	Hospital	in	Kurinjipadi, we have added state-of-the-art trauma and emergency care wards, delivering enhanced critical medical services	to	communities	in	a	time-sensitive	manner.	To	extend specialised assistance, we formalised an MoU with CHILDS Trust Hospital, Chennai, demonstrating NLCIL’s commitment to supporting vulnerable segments of society through	partnerships	with	premier	healthcare	institutions.
Underpinning	these	efforts,	major	capital	injections—
amounting	to	nearly	₹48.63	crore	(including	₹1.44	crore	for EC Compliance) in FY 2024-25—were allocated across healthcare infrastructure, community outreach, and	medical	programming.	These	resources	have	enabled	an	impressively	broad	reach:	free	outpatient	(OP)	and	emergency treatment services delivered in tens of thousands of instances each year, covering more than 110,000	rural	consultations	annually.
Beyond medical interventions, NLCIL has played a critical 
role in supporting national health priorities—most notably, our ‘100 Days Eradication Campaign’ under the TB-Free India initiative, which included administering preventative medications, diagnostic services, and pro-health messaging via mobile Direct Digital Oath (“Ni-kshay Shapath”) initiatives.
These	efforts	collectively	underscore	our	belief	that	
health	should	not	be	a	privilege,	but	an	assured	right.	By empowering local healthcare ecosystems via enduring institutions and delivering compassionately through partnerships, NLCIL continues to reinforce its role as a vigilant	and	caring	custodian	of	community	well-being.

Supplier Ecosystem
Suppliers play an essential role in sustaining NLCIL’s 
operations across mining, power generation, and renewable energy	projects.	The	company	engages	a	wide	base	of suppliers for critical inputs such as heavy mining machinery, lignite handling systems, thermal power plant equipment,	flue	gas	desulphurisation	units,	electrostatic	precipitators,	and	components	for	solar	and	wind	projects. A	significant	proportion of suppliers are local and regional contractors, supporting employment and economic development in Tamil Nadu, Rajasthan, and Odisha, where NLCIL has major	operations.
Beyond transactional engagement, NLCIL focuses on building long-term supplier reliability by monitoring quality, delivery performance, and compliance with safety	and	environmental	standards.	With	the	ongoing	expansion of renewable energy capacity, the supplier network is also diversifying to include technology providers in solar modules, inverters, wind turbines, and	battery	storage	solutions. Responsible Mining and Power Generation
At NLC India Limited, we acknowledge that our role 
as a lignite miner and power producer carries with it a duty	of	care	towards	the	environment.	Mining	and	power	generation, by their very nature, have an ecological impact, and we therefore approach these activities with a strong sense	of	responsibility.	Our	long-standing	commitment	has	been to reduce this impact through cleaner technologies, efficient	processes,	and	sustainable	practices,	while	aligning	with	India’s	ambition	of	achieving	net	zero	by	2070.
Over the years, we have progressively embedded modern 
emission-control systems, advanced monitoring tools, and energy-efficiency	measures	across	our	mining	and	thermal	operations.	These	actions	have	enabled	us	to	steadily	lower	energy	intensity	and	minimise	air	and	water	emissions.	Yet, recognising that the challenges of climate change require more than incremental improvements, we have now begun	to	invest	in	transformative	solutions	that	can	redefine	the	environmental	profile	of	our	business.
In FY 2024–25, we entered into a binding Memorandum 
of Understanding with the Indian Institute of Technology Madras to jointly pursue research and development in Advance	Carbon	Capture	Systems	(CCS).	This	partnership	represents a critical step towards addressing hard-to-abate emissions, with the potential to establish scalable models for	carbon	mitigation	in	India.	In	parallel,	we	are	advancing	projects to convert lignite into methanol and exploring the production of green hydrogen—initiatives that reimagine the role of lignite not merely as a conventional fuel, but as a	pathway	towards	cleaner	energy	alternatives.
We are also shaping the future of renewable energy 
integration.	Through	our	subsidiary,	NLC	India	Renewables	Ltd (NIRL), we secured a landmark 250 MW/500 MWh Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) project in Tamil Nadu, awarded by Tamil Nadu Green Energy Corporation Ltd.	Once	operational,	this	will	be	one	of	the	largest	storage	projects in the country, enabling greater penetration of renewable power and strengthening grid stability while directly	contributing	to	the	reduction	of	carbon	emissions.
Governance	underpins	these	efforts.	Our	dedicated	
ESG Committee continues to steer strategic priorities, embedding environmental considerations into corporate decision-making and ensuring that our actions are in line with global standards such as the Science Based Targets initiative	(SBTi)	Net	Zero	Standard.	This	framework	provides	a	clear	and	scientifically	grounded	trajectory	for	our	decarbonisation	journey.
Alongside	these	flagship	initiatives,	we	maintain	our	focus 	
on	the	responsible	use	of	natural	resources.	We	recycle	and 	
reuse	water	across	our	operations,	promote	fly	ash	utilisation 	
in cement and infrastructure, and undertake extensive 
reclamation	and	afforestation	programmes	in	mined-out 	
areas.	Biodiversity	studies	within	and	around	our	campuses 	
guide	our	efforts	to	conserve	native	ecosystems,	ensuring	that 	
development	is	balanced	with	ecological	preservation. 	
We have also initiated the conversion of Overburden (OB) into Manufactured Sand (M-Sand), reducing the pressure on	riverbed	mining	while	enabling	sustainable	construction. 	
We are also repurposing reclaimed mined-out lands for the establishment	of	solar	power	plants	for	the	first	time	in	the 	
country, creating a model for clean energy generation on post-mining	landscapes.
By combining pioneering projects with responsible 
operations, NLCIL is demonstrating that mining and power generation can evolve to meet the demands of a low-carbon economy.	Our	responsibility 	is	not	only	to	generate	energy	for	
the nation today, but also to ensure that we do so in a manner that	safeguards	the	environment	for	generations	to	come.

Greenhouse Gas Emissions
We recognise our responsibility to limit greenhouse gas 
(GHG) emissions and align with the nation’s climate goals.	Our	operations,	which	rely	significantly	on	lignite-based	power,	inevitably	generate	emissions.	However,	we are committed to progressively reducing both the scale	and	intensity	of	these	emissions	through	efficiency	improvements, clean technologies, and future-ready solutions	such	as	carbon	capture	and	storage	(CCS).
In	FY	2024-25,	our	Scope	1	emissions	were	30.12	million 	
tCO₂e,	an	increase	from	25.15	million	tCO₂e	in	FY	2023-24. 	
However, emission intensity improved, declining to 
1.08	t/MWh	from	1.16	t/MWh	in	the	previous	year.	This 	
reduction	underscores	the	effectiveness	of	our	operational 	
efficiency	measures,	process	optimisations,	and	the 	
continued adoption of advanced emission control systems across	our	power	stations.	On	the	other	hand,	our	Scope	2 	
emissions were recorded at 44,935 tCO
2e, compared with 
303 tCO2e in the previous year, primarily due to higher 
reliance on grid-supplied electricity for auxiliary and office	operations.	While	our	Scope	2	emissions	remain 	
negligible relative to Scope 1, we continue to improve energy efficiency	in	non-core	operations	by	promoting	renewable 	
energy	adoption	in	our	administrative	facilities.
